groups.text: It is currently a cloudy morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 19 degrees Celsius.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Google is updating its Gemini Flash models to change how artificial intelligence processes video footage. Instead of scanning frames at a fixed rate, the new agent-based analysis allows Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, and 3.5 Flash-Lite to autonomously decide which segments to examine and at what resolution. This shift reduces token usage by up to 88 percent and cuts costs by 66 percent. The system can now identify moments shorter than one second, such as state changes or quick cuts, which Google says makes automated video editing more precise. These models can also track individual scenes across hours of footage and spot anomalies by resampling suspicious windows at higher frame rates. While the feature is currently available through the Gemini API, Google plans to integrate these capabilities into YouTube and the Gemini app at a later date.

Ireland’s Foreign Minister Helen McEntee would not commit to adding the Aughinish Alumina plant to an upcoming EU sanctions list. The facility is owned by the Russian company Rusal and exports the vast majority of its material to Russia. Data published in May by The Irish Times suggests that alumina from the plant has been found in weapons used by Moscow against Ukraine. While the Irish government previously argued that sanctions would harm the EU more than Russia, Dublin eventually launched an investigation. Prime Minister Micheal Martin stated that this probe found no concrete or definitive evidence linking the material to a Russian weapons manufacturer. Minister McEntee noted that the resulting report has been provided to both the European Commission and Ukrainian officials as they continue to work together on the matter.

A massive security breach has exposed the personal data of millions across North America. Cybersecurity expert Bryan Krebs discovered an illegal service called Nexus on a Russian forum that provided access to 153 million American and Canadian driver's licenses. The leak also included 10 million ID cards, two million travel documents, and 600,000 medical cards, likely extracted from an identity verification provider. The FBI has launched an investigation into the matter. Meanwhile, in Thailand, Bangkok has suspended three applications for large stand-alone data centers. Governor Chadchart Sittipunt noted that developers previously registered these facilities as warehouses to avoid environmental impact assessments and industrial licenses. This pause comes as nationwide investment applications in the sector reach 728 billion baht. In Washington, President Trump announced new drug pricing deals with midsize biotechnology companies. Analysts suggest these voluntary agreements may not lower costs for many, as they primarily apply to Medicaid while exempting companies from Medicare price cuts.

The llama.cpp project has released update b10756 to refine how local AI models interact with hardware. The primary change involves Vulkan, where the software now only requests the VK_KHR_shader_bfloat16 extension if it is supported by the system. This technical adjustment supports a wide range of environments across different operating systems. For Apple users, the release includes builds for macOS Apple Silicon with KleidiAI enabled, though Intel-based Macs are currently disabled. Linux users can run the software on Ubuntu via CPU, Vulkan, ROCm 7.14, OpenVINO, or SYCL. Windows support is extensive, covering CUDA versions 12 and 13, alongside OpenVINO and ROCm 7.14. The update also extends to Android arm64 and openEuler systems using aarch64 and x86 architectures. These changes ensure that developers can deploy models more reliably across diverse hardware configurations from mobile devices to high-end workstations.

The European Union is summoning Russia’s envoy in Brussels following a failed attack involving an explosives-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month. Germany's foreign and interior ministers concluded on Tuesday that Russia was responsible for the incident. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated the attempt had all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism. France is taking a similar step, with Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot summoning the Russian charge d'affaires in Paris to protest. While these diplomatic protests unfold, Kallas noted that the EU is continuing work on its next package of some 1,600 sanctions listings related to Russia's war in Ukraine. She suggested that more may be added to those lists in response to the Leipzig attack.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority has officially launched its phase one merger inquiry into E.ON SE's anticipated acquisition of OVO Energy Ltd. This investigation follows a pre-notification period and an invitation for public comment that began in July, with the regulator now working toward a statutory decision deadline of October 28th to determine if the utility deal harms competition. In separate technology news, Mozilla has released Firefox 155 across all platforms, introducing the Smart Window—or Fenêtre intelligente—to users in France, Canada, and the United States. This optional beta feature requires a Firefox account and allows users to summarize pages or compare tabs using various large language models, including Mistral Small 4, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, and Qwen 3 235B. While conversations are stored locally, Mozilla notes that requests transit through its servers and those of the chosen model providers.

The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into daily life is creating new pressures for both corporate security and public health. In the enterprise sector, organizations are scrambling to balance the power of AI tools with necessary guardrails, as agentic AI introduces a new insider threat model for companies. This has led to an increase in specialized training, including virtual events focused on securing cloud assets and building secure AI strategies to manage governance and identity risks. Meanwhile, these same algorithmic influences are raising alarms in the medical community. Experts argue that the next edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, expected in 2030, must address how digital environments and algorithms shape eating disorders. This would be the first revision since 2013, a time before TikTok existed or generative AI served as a source of health information, highlighting a significant gap between psychiatric guidelines and modern digital reality.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain cloudy with rain chances up to 65 percent and temperatures between 17 and 22 degrees Celsius.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Haushaltspflege at 🏚️, at 10:00, Optikrunde, at 13:00, Jovita Meeting, and at 15:00, Gruppenmeeting Gregor.
Mail worth checking: Laura Wiegand sent several inquiries about your wooden pallets on Kleinanzeigen. Also, Amazon reports that your SodaStream order is out for delivery today.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
